records.name: The Crossing
records.summary: A professional chamber choir that sings only new music, commissioning and premiering new works. Most people take part by attending its concerts or buying its recordings.
records.what_you_do: Go to a concert, buy a ticket for the date you pick, or join the email list. The site does not describe auditions, volunteering, classes or community programs.

schedule.text: A season of concerts, mostly from fall to spring. Several each season are in Philadelphia and Chestnut Hill, and others are in other cities.

cost.text: Tickets are sold for each concert. The season page gives no prices, so check each concert's own ticket page.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to one of the upcoming concerts, starting with a Philadelphia date, or join the email list to hear about new dates.
first_step.basis: Concerts are open to the public, and each date has its own ticket page. The site does not describe any way to sing with the choir, so this rating covers attending only.
first_step.what_to_expect: A concert is a seated performance by a professional choir, often in a church. The program is new music, and some concerts include other musicians or staging. The season page does not give the length of a concert, so check the event page before you buy.
first_visit_tips: Use the ticket link on the concert's own page, since prices and seating are set per event.
Check the start time on your event page, because the season ranges from afternoon to evening starts.
Email info@crossingchoir.org with access questions, since the site lists no access details.

records.notes: Tier 1 schedule text named one October 2026 concert. That is now a general description, since one-time dates do not belong there. Tier 1 days value (Sunday) was removed because concert days vary. The contact page gives 8855 Germantown Avenue as the choir's address. It is not recorded as a place the public meets, because no page says so. No page read mentions auditions, volunteering, community programs or open rehearsals. The news page's newest item is dated June 2026. The upcoming page lists 13 concerts for 2026 to 2027, seven of them in Philadelphia. Its last_sign_of_life is the October 2026 concert listing.

records.name: The Friends of Mario Lanza Park
records.summary: Volunteers, formed in 1987, who look after this small historic park in Queen Village. They run regular cleanups and planting days, plus summer events: KidFest in June, Movie Nights in July, and Music Month in September.
records.what_you_do: Join a cleanup or planting day, or help with the summer events. The group asks people to email it to learn how to get involved.

schedule.text: Regular cleanups and planting days, plus a yearly run of summer events: KidFest in June, Movie Nights in July, and Music Month in September. The group's pages give no fixed day or time for work sessions.

cost.text: The group's pages list no cost for volunteering or for the summer events.

first_step.how: Email friends-mariolanzapark@qvna.org and ask about the next cleanup or planting day.
first_step.basis: The group's page invites anyone to email about volunteering, so the way in is clear. No beginner session or regular work-day time is listed, so the rating stays at 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect a hands-on cleanup or planting in the park, done by volunteers. The pages do not say how long a session runs or what to bring. Email first to confirm the date and to ask those questions.
first_visit_tips: Email the group before you come, since no regular work-day times are posted.
Ask the group what to bring, because the pages list no tools or clothing.

records.notes: The QVNA events page lists KidFest (June 2026) and Mario at the Movies (July 2026) dates at this park. Those set last_sign_of_life. No Music Month date appears. Love Your Park cleanups on the same page are at other parks and are not used here. The QVNA volunteer page has a form that does not load on the cached page, so email is the only contact that could be checked. One WebSearch found no 2026 cleanup date for this park. Confidence raised from low to medium because the group's own pages and the events calendar now agree.

records.name: The Friends of Sedgley Woods
records.summary: Volunteers who look after Sedgley Woods, a 27-hole disc golf course in Fairmount Park. They run monthly workdays, weekly rounds, and monthly singles tournaments, and playing the course is always free.
records.what_you_do: Help with course upkeep at the second Saturday workday, or play the weekly rounds and the monthly singles tournaments.

schedule.text: Workdays on the second Saturday of each month, 9 am to noon, with tag results at 1 pm. Weekly tags on Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays all year: Saturday and Sunday start at 11 am, and Thursday start times are set by sunset. Monthly pro/am singles tournaments. The course is open from sunup to sundown.

cost.text: Playing the course is always free. The monthly singles events are described as low cost, and the site does not give an entry fee.

first_step.how: Come to the second Saturday workday, 9 am to noon, at the course, or email friendsofsedgleywoods@gmail.com to ask how to join.
first_step.basis: The course page says a club member is usually on site to answer questions and show newcomers around. It names two easy ways in: a monthly workday or an email. The tags and monthly events are described as casual.
first_step.what_to_expect: A workday is a few hours of outdoor work: mowing, weed-whacking, picking up sticks and trash, and course projects. Weekend tags start at 11 am, so arrive early to check in. Discs are usually sold at the course on Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays, and play is free.
first_visit_tips: Check the group's Facebook page or email before a workday, because workdays are sometimes moved or canceled.
For a weekend tag, arrive early to check in.
Ask a club member on site where to start, since the page says one is usually around to help newcomers.

records.notes: The last_sign_of_life and its URL are carried from tier 1 (the city Friends list). This pass found no month-dated item on the group's own pages. The tag schedule and events calendar are linked as 2026 items, but the readable text gives no month, and the 2026 Thursday schedule is an image that could not be read. Tier 1 summary said the group was founded in 1977. The About page says the group formed in 1990, after ten of the original baskets were stolen, so the summary no longer gives a founding year. The 1977 date may refer to the course, which no page read here dates. Membership exists ('members in good standing' elect the board each December), but dues and requirements are not described, so no membership fields are set. The course pages do not describe parking, restrooms or wheelchair access.

records.name: The German Society of Pennsylvania
records.summary: A heritage society founded in 1764 to help German immigrants. It now runs German classes, a public library, and monthly conversation evenings, film nights and book clubs for anyone who wants to learn German or enjoy German culture.
records.what_you_do: Take a German class, join the monthly conversation evening or a film night, or join a book club. Members get library borrowing and invitations to special events.

schedule.text: The monthly Konversationsabend, a German conversation evening, is on the second Wednesday from 6 to 8 pm, February to May and September to December. Friday film nights start at 6:30 pm during the film season. German classes run in terms of about 8 to 12 weeks. Yearly events include the Stiftungsfest gala, a Christkindlmarkt, and St. Martin's Parade.

cost.text: Regular 10-week classes cost $360, and the 8-week online classes cost $180 to $240. Textbooks cost about $30 to $70 extra, and private tutoring is $45 an hour. Membership dues start at $30 for students and $60 for individuals. The membership page does not say which year these apply to.

access.notes: The main entry is through the parking lot door on the east side. An elevator entrance is on the Spring Garden side, so call ahead during business hours so staff can unlock the gate. Nearest SEPTA: the Frankford Elevated ('the El'), at the Spring Garden Street stop about five blocks east of the building.

first_step.how: Sign up for the mailing list, then come to the second-Wednesday Konversationsabend from 6 to 8 pm.
first_step.basis: The conversation evening page says newcomers from any background are welcome, from beginner to advanced speakers, and it explains how to sign up. The class page offers courses from beginner to advanced, with a free level change in the first three weeks.
first_step.what_to_expect: About 20 people meet around a set theme. A speaker gives a short talk, then the group talks it over, with refreshments. The page does not list a price for the conversation evening, and classes are paid per term.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for the mailing list first, since that is how the group announces the evening.
Park only in the Society's own lot behind the black gate, not under the mural, because cars there risk being towed.
The library is open Tuesday and Thursday from 10 am to 4 pm, and the offices are open weekdays from 9 am to 5 pm.

records.notes: Membership price conflict: the classes page says membership is $30, while the membership page lists $30 for students only and $60 for individuals. The record uses the membership page figures. The membership page gives no year for its prices. Tier 1 said membership comes before classes. The class page does not say membership is required, so the first step now points to the conversation evening. The Konversationsabend location is given as the Ratskeller, but the page gives no address for it, so no extra location was added. The events page names monthly events without dates. The 2026 to 2027 dates are on the monthly events page. Tier 1 last_sign_of_life (2025-11) is replaced by the October 2026 film listing. Tier 1 online_ok was false, but some classes and tutoring are online, so it is now true. The 1764 founding year is carried over from tier 1; the About page was not read in this pass. Tier 1 2025 gala price was dropped from cost text because it was a one-time event. The Stiftungsfest 2026 page exists, but its date was not shown on the pages read.

records.name: The Head & The Hand
records.summary: A nonprofit independent publisher and community bookstore on Frankford Avenue. It runs a writing group, a poetry book club, author events and readings, and it lets community groups book its lower-level workshop for free.
records.what_you_do: Join the writing group or the Poetry is for Everyone book club, go to an author event or reading, donate books for store credit, or book the workshop for a community meeting.

schedule.text: A writing group about once a month on a Saturday or Sunday afternoon, 2 to 3:30 pm. The Poetry is for Everyone book club meets monthly on Sunday afternoons, 2 to 3 pm. Both meet at Valerio Coffee Roasters. The store also hosts author events and a children's story time.

cost.text: The events page gives no price for the writing group or the book club, and registration is usually required. Author events vary: some are free or pay what you can, and others are ticketed.

access.notes: The lower-level community workshop is reached by a stairwell, according to the group's booking page.

first_step.how: Register on the events page for the next writing group session or Poetry is for Everyone book club meeting, then go to the venue named on that listing.
first_step.basis: The writing group is open to writers of any genre and career stage, and the book club reads one poetry book at each meeting. Both say to register on each event page, so the way in is clear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The writing group meets for about 90 minutes with writers at any stage. The poetry book club meets for an hour, and members read and discuss one book at each meeting. Prices are not listed for these meetings, and registration is usually needed.
first_visit_tips: Register through the event page before you go, since registration is required for the writing group.
Call 267-702-6744 or email info@theheadandthehand.com for directions, parking or transit, since the site gives none.
Check the events page for changes, because one book club meeting was rescheduled and its new date is still to be set.

records.notes: Name changed from 'The Head & The Hand Workshop' (tier 1) to the name the group's own site uses. 'Workshop' is the name of its lower-level space. Status moved from probably_active to active because the events list runs March to November 2026. last_sign_of_life is September 2026, the newest listed date on or before 2026-10-08. The monthly Personal Velocity reading series is listed for August 2025 to August 2026, so it may have ended, and it is left out of the schedule text. The writing group and book club meet at Valerio Coffee Roasters. Its address is not on the site, so it is not a location record. Book donations: staff review each book, and store credit covers up to half the price of a used book. Textbooks and advance reader copies are not taken. The site gives no store hours and no parking, transit or wheelchair details. Community workshop bookings need 5 days' notice and do not cover private parties or public events. One events listing had a day mismatch (a Sourland event shown as Wednesday and Tuesday), so it was not used.

records.name: The Historical Society of Frankford
records.summary: A volunteer-run history group, founded in 1905, that keeps and shares the history of Frankford. It holds monthly lectures, runs a museum open by appointment, and offers library research help.
records.what_you_do: Attend a free lecture at the Society's building, book a museum visit or research help, or watch past lectures on the Society's YouTube channel.

schedule.text: Monthly evening lectures from March to June and from September to December. Doors open at 7 pm and the talk starts at 7:30 pm. The lectures are also streamed live on the Society's Facebook page. The museum is open by appointment.

cost.text: Lectures are free and open to the public. Museum visits are by appointment, and the site lists no admission fee.

access.notes: Lectures are streamed live on the Society's Facebook page for people who cannot attend in person.

first_step.how: Come to a free monthly lecture at 1507 Orthodox Street. Doors open at 7 pm and the talk starts at 7:30 pm.
first_step.basis: Lectures are free, open to the public, and posted with a set time and place. The site does not describe any newcomer welcome beyond that, so the rating is 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: A lecture is a single evening talk in the Society's building, with doors at 7 pm and the talk at 7:30 pm. The Society's notice for its October lecture says light refreshments are served and masks are optional. You can also watch a lecture live online.
first_visit_tips: Park in the free lot across Orthodox Street at Frankford Friends School.
Arrive when doors open at 7 pm, so you are settled before the 7:30 pm talk.
Call 215-743-6030 to ask about the next lecture or to book a museum visit.

records.notes: The site's events page and membership page both returned 404 (listed under blocked). The About page says membership is open to anyone but gives no dues or benefits. The museum page has a phone line and a Write Us form, but no email. The schedule text leaves out the October 13, 2026 lecture because one-time events do not belong there. The interest tag preservation_architecture is kept from tier 1 as the nearest fit for a local history society, since no exact tag exists. The 1905 founding year comes from the About page. Frankford CDC is named as a partner on the Society's community page and is listed under leads_only.

records.name: The Lady Hoofers Tap Ensemble
records.summary: A Philadelphia tap company, founded in 2011, that makes its own tap work and stages a holiday show each December. It runs a Class Series, a Youth Ensemble for young women ages 9 to 18, and free tap lessons for students at a Philadelphia elementary school.
records.what_you_do: Take a Class Series session at the intermediate or advanced level, audition for the Youth Ensemble each spring, see The Tapcracker holiday show, or ask about the company's free school tap programs.

schedule.text: Class Series sessions run on Sunday afternoons, in two four-week sessions: 3 to 4 pm for teens and adults ages 15 and up, and 4 to 5 pm for youth ages 9 and up. The Youth Ensemble rehearses on Sundays through the fall and holds auditions each spring. The Tapcracker holiday show runs each December.

cost.text: Tapcracker tickets run $35 to $65 by seat section. The site does not list fees for the Class Series, the Youth Ensemble, or school programs, so ask through the website contact form.

access.notes: At the Tapcracker venue, the orchestra and mezzanine seats can be reached without stairs. Accessible seating can be requested by emailing the box office.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to The Tapcracker, the December holiday show, to see the company before you take a class.
first_step.basis: The Class Series is listed only at intermediate and advanced levels. The Youth Ensemble is by audition, and most successful applicants have at least three years of training. No beginner class is listed, so the way in for a true beginner is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Tapcracker is a ticketed holiday show with four performances over one December weekend. A Class Series session is one hour on a Sunday afternoon, for four weeks. The Youth Ensemble is pre-professional, so expect serious training rather than a casual class.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for the newsletter through the site's sign-up link to hear when Class Series registration opens on December 2.
Everyone needs a ticket to The Tapcracker, and children under three are not admitted.
All sales are final, and the show goes on rain or shine with no weather refunds.
For accessible seating, email the box office, since the orchestra and mezzanine seats avoid stairs.

records.notes: Tier 1 first step pointed to the Email Us page. That page is a general contact form with no email address, so the first step now points to the show ticket, and the newsletter sign-up is in the tips. Tier 1 last_sign_of_life (2026-10) came from the December 2026 show listings, which are upcoming, so it is replaced by May 2026, the youth audition date on the Youth Ensemble page. The Class Series page gives dates with no year, so no year is written for them. The class studio address is not on any page read, so no class location is recorded. Accessibility details cover the show venue only. Class and ensemble prices are not published.
